title: Isolation guardrails for heterogeneous GPU fleets — PRD (idea)
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a product proposal for runtime "isolation guardrails" tailored to heterogeneous GPU fleets in Redwood Dedicated. Goal: enable safe, predictable tenant isolation while preserving high utilization across mixed hardware (multiple GPU types and shapes), supporting burst windows, and integrating with autoscaling policies. This is an exploratory PRD/idea doc — simulation and SRE experiments required before full spec.

Context / problem statement:
- Customers reserve Dedicated capacity across pools that may contain mixed GPU generations (A100, H100, L40) and flavors (different memory, nvlink topologies).
- Mixed fleets are cost-efficient but increase noisy-neighbor risk and make eviction/preemption decisions brittle: thermal hotspots, PCIe congestion, NUMA effects cause long-tail latency spikes.
- Current tenant isolation knobs are coarse: hard quota, soft throttle, or full preemption. These lead to suboptimal outcomes: underutilized capacity to avoid interference, or tenant SLA violations during bursts.
- Need a middle ground: guardrails that are aware of hardware heterogeneity, thermal and topology constraints, and that integrate with autoscale/burst economics so we both protect SLAs and improve utilization.

High-level proposal (what we want):
1) Per-pool topology awareness: the allocator maintains a lightweight topology map (GPU type, NVLink clusters, PCIe lanes, NUMA zones, vendor metrics) and exposes a small set of labels that the scheduler and autoscaler can use.
2) Isolation profiles (tenant-facing): tenants choose a profile per-reservation: "strict-isolate" (strongly prefer dedicated card, minimal co-tenancy), "balanced" (prefer isolation but allow co-tenancy with soft QoS), "opportunistic" (maximize throughput, tolerate preemption).
3) Thermal and PCIe-aware microplacement: before starting a burst allocation, runtime checks thermal headroom, memory pressure, and recent tail-latency signals; it shifts allocations within pool if a better topology exists.
4) Fractional burst credits: tenants get a small burst allowance (fractional units) that can be consumed for short windows; credits decay with configurable half-life. Credits are reserved across similar-arch groups to avoid cross-architecture fragmentation.
5) Soft-fence eviction ladder: eviction occurs in stages — throttle -> partial preempt (pause lowest-priority tasks) -> full preempt. Each stage has time windows and user-visible signals.
6) Autoscaler integration: autoscaler policies can request topology-aware warmup (spin up specific GPU types) when demand for a tenant profile is predicted.

Goals (success criteria):
- Customers on "balanced" profile see <1% increase in tail latency (p99) vs isolated baseline during normal ops, while utilization of mixed pools improves by 8–15% in simulations.
- Burst-request success rate (allocation satisfied without fallbacks) > 95% for top 50 tenants in pilot.
- No silent QoS regressions: every soft throttle is observable in Console and traceable to tenant + topology.

Non-goals:
- This doc does not propose heavy-weight per-VM cgroups or kernel-level changes. We rely on runtime-level QoS and placement policies.
- Not addressing instance lifecycle / hardware procurement process (that's infra ops).

Detailed requirements:
Functional:
- Allocator must store and serve a topology descriptor per node: GPU model, memory, NVLink clusters, PCIe/gpu adjacency, and thermal headroom estimate (string).
- Tenant reservation API: include isolation_profile (one of strict-isolate|balanced|opportunistic), burst_window_seconds (int), burst_credit_rate (float).
- Autoscaler API: allow hinting target GPU families and a warmup_deadline to request prewarming for predicted bursts.
- Runtime placement: prefer same-arch placement for cache-sensitive workloads, avoid pairing H100 with low-memory cards for memory-bound tenants.
- Telemetry: emit events for topology-influenced moves, thermal-throttle events, and credit consumption.

Operational / observability:
- Console: per-tenant isolation profile view, credit balance timeline, topology heatmap (hot nodes), recent relocations with reason codes.
- Alerts: when >5% of allocations in pool were relocated due to thermal constraints within 1h.
- Runbook: steps for manual intervention (drain node, reassign pool labels, throttle burst-credit issuance).

UX & API sketch:
- PATCH /dedicated/reservations/:id { "isolation_profile": "balanced", "burst_credit_rate": 0.25 }
- Console toggles for default pool-profile, with explanations: "Strict: reserved card, best latency; Balanced: good latency with higher utilization; Opportunistic: best throughput; may be preempted"
- In Allocation response include fields: allocated_topology_label, credit_remaining_seconds, expected_preemption_window

Autoscaler behavior:
- Predictive warmup: when predicted demand for a geographic pool crosses threshold, autoscaler will 1) request specific GPU families, 2) request pre-warm of NVLink clusters (simulate with warm containers), 3) mark nodes as preferred for isolated profiles.
- Scaling-down: avoid immediate decommit if any tenant in pool has positive burst credits or active relocation history in last 15 minutes.

Operator controls / guardrails:
- Pool-level soft cap: define a utilization threshold per topology group; above threshold, block opportunistic allocations and drain non-critical workloads.
- Emergency thermal window: if node thermal headroom < X, automatically relocate opportunistic workloads off the node and move balanced workloads only with operator approval.

Simulations & experiments needed (next steps):
- Run mixed-workload stochastic simulator (existing capacity-sim) updated to model thermal coupling, NVLink contention, and credit consumption. Target: synthetic workload set of 200 tenants mixing chat, embeddings, and long-context inference.
- Pilot against a small dedicated lab pool containing A100+H100+L40 nodes — instrument long-tail latency and eviction ladder.
- A/B on two pilot customers: offer "balanced" vs "strict" by default and measure utilization/cost.

Metrics to monitor:
- Allocation success rate (burst requests satisfied) per profile
- p50/p95/p99 latency delta pre/post-relocation
- Pool utilization by topology group
- Credit consumption rate and average credit balance
- Number of relocations per tenant per day, broken down by reason (thermal|topology|autoscale)

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Overcomplicated allocator logic increases bug surface. Mitigation: implement feature flags, limit to small lab pools first, and provide operator override.
- Risk: Customers misunderstand profiles and pick opportunistic when they need strict latency. Mitigation: UX copy, default conservative mode, trial warnings.
- Risk: Thermal model inaccurate leading to oscillations. Mitigation: smooth measurements (sliding windows), hysteresis, and safe fallback to throttle-only mode.

Open questions:
- How fine-grained should topology descriptors be? (simple family tag vs detailed NVLink graph)
- Should credits be transferable between tenants in same org (economics)?
- How to price fractional burst credits? flat fee vs usage-based?

Acceptance criteria for MVP:
- Topology descriptor and labeling in allocator implemented.
- Tenant API supports isolation_profile and burst_credit_rate.
- Telemetry for relocations and credit usage emitted and visible in Console.
- Small-lab pilot shows utilization improvement >= 6% with p99 tail latency increase <= 2% for balanced profile.

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Sim workplan (Ethan) — update capacity sim with thermal model (due 2025-03-24)
- API schema PR (Priya) — draft API change and UX copy (due 2025-03-21)
- Infra lab setup (Liam) — provision mixed GPU pool and baseline metrics (due 2025-03-28)

Notes / todo / rough ideas (brainstorm snippets):
- Could tie burst credits to billing tokens so customers can auto-purchase if they exhaust credits.
- Consider per-tenant noise budgets derived from historical tail-latency sensitivity tests.
- Short-term: implement only topology family tags, then iterate to include NVLink clusters after first pilot.
- Consider a read-only "topology simulator" in Console where customers can preview placement decisions.

References:
- Related infra ticket: ENG-5368 (topology metadata service)
- Prototype allocator PR: github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/912

End of draft — feedback requested from product, infra, serving-runtime, and SRE.
